lesson.explanation: Multiply matching coordinates, then add those products. The result is one number.
lesson.connection: Attention compares a query with each key using a dot product.

lesson.explanation: Each output entry is a dot product of a row on the left and a column on the right. Inner dimensions must match.
lesson.connection: QK^T computes many query-key dot products at once.

lesson.explanation: Exponentiate each score, then divide each exponential by their sum. This makes positive weights that sum to one. For large scores, subtract the largest score before exponentiating.
lesson.worked_example: Scores [0, ln(2)] have exponentials [1,2]. Divide by 3 to get [1/3,2/3].
lesson.connection: Attention applies softmax to each row of scaled query-key scores.

lesson.explanation: Multiply every coordinate of each vector by its own weight, then add coordinate by coordinate. Do not add the vectors first.
lesson.connection: An attention output mixes value vectors with their attention weights; it does not just pick the largest weight.

lesson.explanation: Take each query-key dot product, then divide by the square root of the key dimension. Use the given dimension, even when a toy example lists only nonzero coordinates.
lesson.worked_example: If q dot k = 12 and d_k = 4, the scaled score is 12 / sqrt(4) = 6.
lesson.connection: Scaling controls the size of logits before softmax produces attention weights.

lesson.explanation: Apply softmax separately to each row of scores. Exponentiate, then normalize; the row sums to one.
lesson.worked_example: For one score row [ln(2),ln(3)], exponentials [2,3] become weights [0.4,0.6].
lesson.connection: Each query has its own distribution over the keys.

attention_output.title: Attention output
attention_output.connection: Each output row is a weighted sum of value rows

lesson.explanation: Multiply each value vector by its matching attention weight and add the scaled vectors.
lesson.connection: Matrix multiplication of the attention-weight matrix by V performs this mixture for every query.

lesson.explanation: Attention has three operations: scaled query-key dot products, row-wise softmax, then a weighted sum of values.
lesson.worked_example: Equal scaled scores [0,0] give weights [0.5,0.5]. With values [4,0] and [0,8], the output is [2,4].
lesson.connection: This is one attention head. Multiple heads learn different projections and their outputs are combined.
